theory: Qualify the intro and facts claiming that none is always a single tree path: this holds for a tree grouping each stage into success and failure, but a tree retaining multiple non-success outcomes can have several none paths. Likewise, seven at-least-one paths assumes three binary stages. Independence means previous results do not change a stage's probability; it does not mean different stages have equal probabilities, as practice.development[0–2] demonstrate.
summary: Replaced five off-booklet tasks with supported probability questions, updated their structure slugs and source citations, and repaired the distractor explanations in q5 and dq-5835, changing one distractor value in dq-5835.
